corpusSummary: This corpus comprises 2026 social-science papers examining how large language models intersect with human behavior, learning, health, and policy. Across fields, authors map cognition, bias, and embodiment gaps; explore AI’s roles in education, counseling, governance, and public participation; and investigate LLM-enabled research methods, simulations, and analytics. Recurring concerns center on trust, safety, equity, and the need for transparent, responsible use.

themes.name: Embodiment and epistemic limits of LLMs
themes.description: Papers consistently show LLMs remain disembodied and struggle to access embodied, sensory, and culturally situated knowledge, heightening concerns about anthropomorphism and misinterpretation.

themes.name: AI in learning, health, and governance: trust, safety, and ethics
themes.description: Studies address AI use in education, health, and public participation, highlighting trust, safety, equity, and governance challenges across contexts.

themes.name: AI as research tool and methodological frontier
themes.description: A wave of work uses LLMs for coding, analysis, simulations, and policy research, while calling for validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: Social dynamics of AI adoption and interaction
themes.description: Research maps how social networks, peer effects, device embodiment, and identity influence AI adoption, consultation, and collaboration.
